findings.title: tests/fixtures/manifest.json has no automated validation of its own shape or content
findings.description: manifest.json is the sole registry of Docker-fixture metadata (name/language/source/path/adapters) and is consumed only by skill/scripts/run_fixture_tests.py, which at run time checks solely whether each `path` exists inside a built image - it never validates the JSON's own required keys, that each `adapters` entry names a real, registered adapter (the set in scripts/run_tools.py / scripts/tools/__init__.py), or that entries stay consistent with what Dockerfile.fixtures actually clones (e.g. the AspGoat/RailsGoat clone URLs and refs live independently in Dockerfile.fixtures, not in this manifest). No file under tests/ imports or asserts against manifest.json at all.
findings.impact: A typo'd or renamed adapter name, a stale fixture path, or drift between this manifest and Dockerfile.fixtures would go undetected by the fast, always-run pytest suite (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `pytest tests/ -q`) - it would only surface, if ever, during a manual, Docker-dependent `run_fixture_tests.py` run, and even then only as a silently-missing entry rather than a test failure.
findings.remediation: Add a lightweight unit test that loads manifest.json and asserts each fixture entry has the required keys and that every listed adapter name exists in the registered adapter set, so drift is caught in CI rather than only in the opt-in Docker harness.

provenance.confirmation_reasoning: Verified independently. (1) The only consumer of tests/fixtures/manifest.json in the repo is skill/scripts/run_fixture_tests.py (MANIFEST = REPO_ROOT / 'tests' / 'fixtures' / 'manifest.json', line 13). Its load_manifest() only checks file existence and JSON syntax (json.JSONDecodeError -> sys.exit(1)); it never validates required keys — it dereferences fixture['name'] and fixture['language'] directly at line 117 and f['name'] in check_fixtures(), which would raise KeyError rather than report a schema error. (2) The 'adapters' key present on every manifest entry is never read by ANY code in the repo: run_fixture_tests.py uses only 'path' (check_fixtures) and 'name'/'language' (printing). I grepped the whole tree; nothing resolves those names against the adapter registry in skill/scripts/tools/__init__.py (ADAPTERS = pip-audit, npm-audit, osv-scanner, eslint-security, semgrep, bandit, trivy, gitleaks, gosec, eslint, brakeman, bundler-audit, spotbugs, dependency-check, cargo-audit, roslyn-secguard). The six adapter names currently listed all happen to exist, but nothing enforces that. (3) Drift with Dockerfile.fixtures is real: the clone URLs and refs (RAILS_GOAT_REF, WEB_GOAT_REF, ASP_GOAT_REF; OWASP/railsgoat, WebGoat/WebGoat, Soham7-dev/AspGoat) live only in Dockerfile.fixtures and are duplicated by hand as 'source' strings in the manifest; nothing cross-checks them. (4) No test asserts against the manifest: grepping tests/ for 'manifest' returns only unrelated hits (tests/tools/test_pip_audit.py dependency-manifest tests, tests/test_synthesize.py:1375 comment, tests/goldens/scout.rendered.txt). tests/test_dockerfile.py and tests/test_assets.py do not touch it. The language integration tests (tests/tools/test_ruby_integration.py, test_java_integration.py, test_csharp_integration.py, test_rust_integration.py) hardcode their own fixture directory names off FIXTURE_ROOT and self.skipTest() when absent — they never read the manifest, so a stale manifest entry produces a silent skip, exactly as the claim states. (5) The always-run CI job is `python -m pytest tests/ -q` (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 41), which therefore covers none of this. Two minor imprecisions that do not change the verdict: load_manifest DOES validate JSON well-formedness (the claim implies only path checking), and the claim cites 'scripts/run_tools.py' / 'scripts/tools/__init__.py' when the real repo paths are skill/scripts/run_tools.py and skill/scripts/tools/__init__.py (that prefix is the import root, so the module names are right). Severity LOW / category test_design is appropriate: this is a dev-only Docker harness, not production code.

findings.title: Module-level test_multi_model_fields_in_schemas is invisible to unittest's own discovery
findings.description: tests/test_schemas.py defines every other test as a method on a unittest.TestCase subclass, but `test_multi_model_fields_in_schemas` (line 257) is a bare module-level function using plain `assert` statements. The file ends with the standard `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` idiom (lines 274-275), and unittest's TestLoader only collects TestCase subclasses via `loadTestsFromModule` - it never discovers top-level `test_*` functions. The test only executes today because CI runs pytest (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` -> `python -m pytest tests/ -q`), which does collect bare functions; any invocation via plain `unittest` (`python tests/test_schemas.py`, or `python -m unittest tests.test_schemas`) silently runs zero of this function's five assertions with no error or skip reported.

findings.title: GitHub Actions step uses a mutable tag or branch reference. Tags and branch names can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks — as seen in the trivy-action and kics-github-action compromises. Pin the reference to a full 40-character commit SHA instead, e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@8ade135a41bc03ea155e62e844d188df1ea18608`.
